subjects.name: Rush Revere and the Brave Pilgrims

summary: A reading of Rush Revere and the Brave Pilgrims, a 2013 time-travel children's book by talk radio host Rush Limbaugh that retells the 1620 Mayflower voyage to sell American exceptionalism and anti-collectivist politics to kids.

evidence.note: book introduced: first Rush Revere novel, Limbaugh caricature on cover
author's note on American exceptionalism picked apart at length
host argues the book indoctrinates children and reflects right-leaning history teaching
individual-and-family framing tied to Thatcher-style anti-collectivism
story opens with the teacher time-travelling to the Mayflower in 1620
class lands near Delfshaven in Holland to meet the Pilgrims
hosts object to the book whitewashing the Puritans as liberty lovers
Mayflower departure from Plymouth, England, with William Bradford
book uses Plymouth common farming as a lesson against collectivism

notes: Short reading; most airtime is mockery of the time-travel plot and classroom scenes. Covered span follows the book's 1620 Pilgrim setting through its 2013 publication, matching other media-reading records. Limbaugh's dates are from general knowledge (the packet only notes he has died). colonialism-imperialism is light: genocide jokes and Puritan whitewashing, a few minutes in total.
